blocks.content: In daily life, we use the word ‘work’ very casually. But in Physics, work has a very specific meaning.
In Physics, work is said to be done only when:
1. A force is applied on an object

items: The displacement is in the direction of force

blocks.content: If any one of these conditions is not satisfied, then NO WORK is done.
Examples of Work

items:
• A boy pushing a car and it moves → Work is done
  • A person lifting a load → Work is done
  • A person pushing a wall → No work (no displacement)
  • A coolie carrying a load on head → No work (force is vertical, motion is horizontal)
A boy pushing a car and it moves → Work is done
A person lifting a load → Work is done
A person pushing a wall → No work (no displacement)
A coolie carrying a load on head → No work (force is vertical, motion is horizontal)

blocks.content: Formula of Work
Work = Force × Displacement W = F×s
SI Unit of Work = Joule (J)
1 Joule is the work done when a force of 1 Newton moves an object through 1 meter in the direction of force.
Types of Work
When force and displacement are in the same direction. Example: A falling object.
When force and displacement are in opposite directions.
Example: Friction acting on a moving body.
When displacement is zero or force is perpendicular. Example: Carrying a bag on the head.
ENERGY

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Work is defined as the dot product of force and displacement: W = F × s × cos(θ).
Work done is zero when displacement is zero or when force and displacement are perpendicular (θ = 90°).
Kinetic Energy is the energy possessed due to motion (KE = 1/2 mv²), whereas Potential Energy is due to position or configuration (PE = mgh).
The Law of Conservation of Energy states that total mechanical energy remains constant in an isolated system.
Power represents the rate of doing work or energy consumption (P = W/t).

blocks.content: Energy is defined as the capacity of a body to do work. Without energy, no work can be performed.
SI unit of energy is Joule (J).
Forms of Energy
Energy exists in various forms such as:

items:
• Mechanical Energy
  • Heat Energy
  • Light Energy
  • Electrical Energy
  • Chemical Energy
  • Sound Energy

blocks.content: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another.
Kinetic Energy
Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Formula:
KE = ½ mv²
Where:
m = mass of body
v = velocity of body
If velocity increases, kinetic energy increases. If mass increases, kinetic energy increases.
Potential Energy
Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or shape. Formula:
PE = mgh
Where:
m = mass
g = acceleration due to gravity

rows: Energy possessed by a body by virtue of its motion
Energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position or shape
Depends on mass, height, and acceleration due to gravity
A moving bullet, flowing water, rolling ball
Water stored in a dam, compressed spring, stretched bow

blocks.content: h = height
Examples:

items:
• Water stored in a dam
  • A stretched spring
  • A raised stone

blocks.content: LAW OF CONSERVATION OF ENERGY
According to this law:
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
It can only be transformed from one form to another.
The total energy of a system always remains constant. Example:
When a ball falls from a height, its potential energy changes into kinetic energy. But the total energy remains the same.
POWER
Power is defined as the rate of doing work. Formula:
Power = Work / Time
SI Unit of Power = Watt (W) 1 Watt = 1 Joule per second
Horse Power
Horse Power (HP) is a bigger unit of power. 1 HP = 746 Watt
It is used for measuring the power of engines and machines.
COMMERCIAL UNIT OF ENERGY
The commercial unit of electrical energy is kilowatt-hour (kWh). 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ Joules

items: Work done by centripetal force is always zero because displacement is perpendicular to the force.
If the momentum of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes 4 times (increases by 300%).
Commercial unit of energy is 1 kWh, which equals 3.6 × 10⁶ Joules.
1 Horsepower (HP) equals 746 Watts, a commonly repeated question in SSC exams.

blocks.content: Electricity bills are calculated in kilowatt-hours.
IMPORTANT SSC EXAM QUESTIONS
Q1. SI unit of work? Ans: Joule
Q2. Formula of kinetic energy? Ans: ½ mv²
Q3. Commercial unit of electricity? Ans: kWh
Q4. SI unit of power?
Ans: Watt
Q5. Law of conservation of energy states?
Ans: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
